work.title: Derive the decided next step in one place and project it onto the board
work.description: The next step a stage result decided is implicit: nextCommand recomputes it from workflow state, and the Project board cannot show it — Status reports what was last attacked, Outcome the terminal result, and nothing says what comes next. Introduce one core derivation — plan, review, build, verify, ship, or done — that every consumer shares, nextCommand first, and project it onto a new single-select Project field reconciled on sync exactly like Status and Outcome. Deliberately not a persisted manifest field: the derivation reads workflow state, so the attribute can never drift from the pipeline it describes.
acceptance: One core derivation yields the decided next step — plan, review, build, verify, ship, or done — for any Work state, and work show exposes it
nextCommand and the Project projection read that same derivation rather than each computing their own
The Project board carries a Next field per Work, created when missing and reconciled on sync like Status and Outcome
A terminal Work shows done on the board, and a sync with no state change edits no field
The projection end-to-end scenario asserts the Next field on the board, and no manifest schema changes

result.handoff:
# Plan: Derive the decided next step in one place and project it onto the board (INIT-4.1)

## Finding (P1)
The Project adapter is already generic — ensureField creates or repairs a single-select field by name (gh-projects.ts:121-149) and ensure() wires Status and Outcome (168-179) — but reconcile() issues item-edit calls unconditionally (199-200), so acceptance 4 ("a sync with no state change edits no field") requires making reconcile drift-aware for all three fields, not merely adding Next. The next step is computed ad hoc only in nextCommand (work-service.ts:99-106); publication's snapshotOf derives Status separately. Nothing is persisted today, and nothing new will be: the derivation reads workflow state (acceptance 5).

## Product files Build touches
1. src/core/types.ts — NEXT_STEPS = ["plan","review","build","verify","ship","done"], type NextStep, and `nextStepOf(work: { completion: unknown; workflow: { stage: Stage } }): NextStep` beside PROJECT_STATUS_BY_STAGE: terminal → "done", otherwise workflow.stage (a return points at its target automatically, since workflow.stage already holds it).
2. src/application/work-service.ts — nextCommand reads nextStepOf for the stage name (its blocked-build special case and null-on-terminal stay; null now comes from next === "done"); WorkView gains `nextStep` via viewOf, so work show exposes it.
3. src/application/ports.ts — GitHubProject gains nextFieldId/nextOptions; GitHubProjects.reconcile gains the next value.
4. src/adapters/gh-projects.ts — NEXT_FIELD ensured in ensure() like the others; reconcile becomes drift-aware: read the item's current Status/Outcome/Next values from the item-list payload and issue item-edit only for fields that differ.
5. src/application/publication.ts — snapshotOf carries nextStepOf(entry) into the publication snapshot; the reconcile call passes it; project status reporting entries gain `next`.
6. src/test/support/github.ts — FakeGitHub: the new reconcile signature, current-value awareness, and edit-call recording so tests can count edits.
7. Tests: src/test/publication.test.ts, src/test/github-projects.test.ts, src/test/work-service.test.ts, plus nextStepOf cases (core-level, in an existing core test file or publication tests — Build's call).
8. scripts/projection-e2e.mjs — assert the Next field after plan (next is review) and at terminal (done); register the assertion string in src/test/documentation.test.ts.

## Rules (P2)
- The derivation is the only place that knows the mapping; every consumer imports it (acceptance 2). nextCommand keeps its richer behavior (start vs complete, blocked-build pointer) but never re-derives the stage.
- The board field is exactly the six lowercase tokens — the vocabulary users type on the CLI.
- Drift-aware reconcile covers all three fields: the no-edit guarantee is a pipeline property, not a Next-only special case.
- No manifest schema change, no new stored attribute (acceptance 5): the field is a projection of workflow state, recomputed on every sync.

## Tests (P3)
1. work show exposes nextStep: ready Work → its stage, active run → the active stage, terminal → done (acceptance 1).
2. nextCommand and the projection agree: after plan completes, nextCommand offers review start and the reconciled Next is review (acceptance 2).
3. Board: a fresh project gains the Next field with the six options; reconcile sets it per Work (acceptance 3).
4. Terminal shows done; a repeated sync with no state change issues zero item-edit calls (acceptance 4, via the Fake's recorded calls).
5. E2E: projection-e2e.mjs checks Next after plan and at terminal; documentation.test.ts registers the string (acceptance 5 is the no-schema-change, asserted by the manifest tests staying untouched and green).

## Acceptance coverage
1. Shared derivation, exposed in work show — types.ts + work-service + test 1.
2. nextCommand and projection read the same derivation — test 2.
3. Next field ensured and reconciled like Status/Outcome — gh-projects + test 3.
4. done at terminal, no edits without change — drift-aware reconcile + test 4.
5. E2E asserts Next; no manifest schema change — E2E + guard + untouched manifest parser tests.

## Verification for Build
npm run verify (typecheck, full unit suite, smoke, --help).

## Non-goals
No persisting of the next step. No board field removal/migration tooling (ensureField's existing repair path covers drifted options). No change to Status/Outcome semantics (INIT-2.3's last-attacked rule stands — Status and Next deliberately differ between stages).

# Review Report: INIT-4.1 Derive the decided next step in one place and project it onto the board

## Verdict
- decision: continue
- rationale: plan is executable, accurate, and completely maps to acceptance criteria.
- return targets: none

## R1 - SPEC-FORMAT / PLAN-FORMAT Audit
The plan breaks the implementation down into a clear DAG of 5 tasks (P1 -> P2 -> P3 -> P4 -> P5). Each acceptance criterion has a directly verifiable mechanism:
1. Core derivation exposed -> `src/core/types.ts` (`nextStepOf`) + `src/application/work-service.ts` (`WorkView.nextStep`); test 1.
2. Both consumers read derivation -> `nextCommand` and `snapshotOf` update; test 2.
3. Board `Next` field created -> `gh-projects.ts` updates leveraging `ensureField`; test 3.
4. Terminal shows done, zero edits on unchanged sync -> `drift-aware reconcile` in `gh-projects.ts` + `FakeGitHub` updates; test 4.
5. E2E asserts Next field, no manifest schema change -> `projection-e2e.mjs` + `documentation.test.ts` update; test 5.

The tasks name the specific files effectively and `npm run verify` is the correct validation command. The blast radius accurately captures the touched files.

## R2 - Repository Validation
The references perfectly mirror `main`:
- `src/adapters/gh-projects.ts`: Lines 121-149 encapsulate `ensureField`. Lines 168-179 encapsulate `ensure`. Lines 199-200 encapsulate unconditional `reconcile` updates.
- `src/application/work-service.ts`: Lines 99-106 encapsulate `nextCommand`, which currently implements an ad-hoc next step switch.
- `src/core/types.ts`: `PROJECT_STATUS_BY_STAGE` exists and is the right neighboring abstraction to `nextStepOf`.
- `src/test/support/github.ts`: `FakeGitHub` implements `reconcile` making it a natural test target for drift-awareness.
- `scripts/projection-e2e.mjs`: Extant script serving E2E assertions for GitHub.

All targets exist and the integration is technically sound without needing schema migrations.
